audit.whatIsWrong: full.diff reads EVEN at 6/10 while Swain wins 55.56% here, and the level chart hands Rumble the majority of stages.
audit.why: The mirror audit (audits/top/rumble__swain.json) reached the same conclusion from the other side: the lane is not even, and Level 1 in particular belongs to Swain on range (Death's Hand 750 / Nevermove 850 vs Flamespitter 600). diff and diffRating are enum fields and exempt from the length band.
audit.corrected: diff FAVOURED, diffRating 4/10, and Level 1 flipped to Swain in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and whys[4] treat Level 6 as a stage Rumble simply takes, and the first-item row is given to Rumble although content.late calls it the most winnable window.
audit.why: The Equalizer is a 130/105/80 second ultimate; at rank 1 that is a 130s window in which Swain's first-item spike plus Nevermove is uncontested. Demonic Ascension also sustains only while draining a champion, so being pushed off the wall is survivable if you root and pull first rather than standing in it.
audit.corrected: First item flipped to Swain, 2+ items flipped to Skill, and the R-vs-Equalizer spike restated around the drain-sustain rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] calls Electro Harpoon 'his short-range E harpoon'; whys[0] and spikes[0] imply Flamespitter simply beats Swain early.
audit.why: Electro Harpoon is 850 range — it matches Nevermove exactly and outranges Death's Hand by 100. Flamespitter is a 600-range cone, so Rumble cannot reach Swain's farming position at all without entering W-speed range. Calling the harpoon short-range tells the player to step up into the one tool that punishes it.
audit.corrected: Harpoon is 850 and matches your root range; Flamespitter is 600 and only lands if you walk in. Level 1 and the early range war belong to Swain.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown number appears anywhere in the matchup for The Equalizer.
audit.why: 130/105/80 seconds is the single most punishable cooldown in the lane and defines when Swain may commit Demonic Ascension safely.
audit.corrected: State 130s at rank 1 and key the first-item all-in to it.

audit.why: The packet flags wants.foe[2] 'Drop Equalizer' as a probable wrong name. It is not — it is correct shorthand for The Equalizer, exactly the false positive class the mirror audit documented. No edit made.

edits.before: W-poke and AA harass win the range war. Identify how Rumble contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Death's Hand at 750 beats his 600 cone, so the range war is yours. His only reply at range is Electro Harpoon, also 850.

edits.before: Rumble opens Level 1 with Flamespitter sustained DPS that trades cleanly into your Q-only kit — farm safely at Q range and give away the level-1 trade entirely.
edits.after: Death's Hand reaches 750 and Flamespitter only 600, so Level 1 is yours — chip him as he steps up to last-hit and never walk into the cone to fish for more.

edits.before: Rumble's Flamespitter sustained DPS trades through your W delay and pre-empts your E root — he overheats on purpose and chunks you before you collect a single fragment.
edits.after: Flamespitter is a 600 cone against your 750 Death's Hand — he wins the early trade only if you step in, so collect fragments from range and refuse every close trade he offers.

edits.before: At Level 6 his Equalizer counters your R drain directly — he places the zone under your feet the moment you transform and the tick damage outpaces your healing unless you root him away from his cast position first.
edits.after: At Level 6 The Equalizer answers your drain — he lays it under your feet the moment you transform, so open with Nevermove at 850 and pull him off his cast spot before you ever toggle Demonic Ascension.

edits.before: Rumble's Equalizer covers the exact zone you need to stand in to drain with R — drop it under you and your healing can't outpace the AOE tick damage.
edits.after: The Equalizer covers the ground you must hold to drain — root and pull him off it first, since Demonic Ascension only lives while you drain a champion.

edits.before: Your Shadowflame or Luden's spike turns W-into-E into a genuine kill threat, but Rumble's Equalizer cooldown and items keep pace — the matchup is close enough that execution decides it.
edits.after: Your Shadowflame or Luden's spike turns W-into-E into a genuine kill threat, and The Equalizer is down 130s at rank 1 — force trades in that window and the first-item stretch is yours.

edits.before: Use W to pre-slow him around terrain so his short-range E harpoon cannot reach you before your E connects
edits.after: Pre-slow with W, then root at 850 — Electro Harpoon matches that range, so step up once he spends both charges

notes: Level chart proposed as matched full/content pairs for the three flipped rows (Level 1, First item, 2+ items). Ratings left alone. Packet suspectName 'Drop Equalizer' in wants.foe[2] is a false positive — correct shorthand — and was not touched, matching the mirror audit's finding. Mirror consistency: rumble__swain.json states Level 1 belongs to Swain but could not flip its own chart row (it left phases[0].side 'Skill' / win[0] 'Rumble'); this file states the same fact from Swain's side, so mirror-fix may need to reconcile the Rumble page's Level 1 row.
